policy: Notes record accessible journal abstracts or authoritative institutional summaries, not completed full-text studies. All notes include source provenance and limits; no new verdict credit until comparative predictions and measured results are examined critically.

notes.label: Hawking: chronology protection
notes.summary: Hawking analyzes whether compactly generated chronology horizons can appear without pathologies, arguing the quantum stress-energy response may obstruct their formation.
notes.limitations: This is a conjecture supported by analysis under assumptions; it is not a general proof forbidding all conceivable backwards travel.
notes.conclusion: Physics of chronology protection is undecided; does not imply either one or multiple branches.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Bothwell et al.: redshift at millimetre scales
notes.summary: An optical atomic clock can resolve differences in gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale sample, a precise test of the Einsteinian prediction.
notes.limitations: Clock comparison concerns relative ticking at different potentials. It is not a trajectory into the past and does not discriminate Everett interpretations.
notes.conclusion: Strengthens established relativistic time dilation only.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Everett: relative state
notes.summary: Everett's work proposes the relative-state formulation of quantum mechanics, important to no-collapse approaches.
notes.limitations: The interpretive account requires connecting universal quantum evolution to experiences; existence of the formulation is not laboratory proof of splitting.
notes.conclusion: Important theoretical hypothesis, zero empirical branch-count credit.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Bell: locality
notes.summary: Bell's theorem establishes testable constraints on a class of local hidden-variable accounts.
notes.limitations: Violations challenge locality assumptions, not automatically single-history interpretations; competing nonlocal or no-collapse theories differ.
notes.conclusion: Crucial falsifiability template, not a direct one-world/many-world test.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Zurek: decoherence
notes.summary: Interactions with the environment suppress interference and favor dynamically robust pointer states, helping explain apparently classical records.
notes.limitations: Decoherence by itself does not uniquely decide whether collapse, hidden variables or many-worlds ontology is correct.
notes.conclusion: Mechanistic explanation reviewed; no direct compass change.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Deutsch: closed timelike quantum lines
notes.summary: Deutsch applies quantum-computation methods to systems interacting with hypothetical closed timelike lines, describing nonclassical consistency behavior.
notes.limitations: The exotic spacetime is assumed in the model; it has not been demonstrated as a travel-accessible physical apparatus.
notes.conclusion: Mathematical model indexed, no observed timeline crossings.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Oreshkov et al.: causal order
notes.summary: A framework allows quantum correlations without preassigned global causal order, highlighting formal alternatives to classical process ordering.
notes.limitations: Indefinite causal order should not be conflated with an observer returning to a prior macroscopic history.
notes.conclusion: New formal questions, not direct multiple-history measurement.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Eagleman: experienced time
notes.summary: Human experience of duration and temporal order is susceptible to measurable distortions and illusions.
notes.limitations: Perceptual anomalies and misordered subjective events do not modify causal spacetime or establish an alternate chronology.
notes.conclusion: Useful category guardrail for neuroscience, neutral to physical branch count.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Hornberger et al.: molecular interference
notes.summary: Interference of relatively complex molecules offers controlled tests of quantum superposition and environmental decoherence.
notes.limitations: Molecular interference supports quantum behavior, not a unique ontology of observed macroscopic branches.
notes.conclusion: High research priority for tests of collapse alternatives, still nondiscriminating here.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Nobel scientific background: biological clocks
notes.summary: Circadian rhythms arise from endogenous genetic and biochemical feedback loops, as documented in Nobel historical material.
notes.limitations: The circadian oscillator tracks and anticipates local day/night cycles, but its biology cannot establish spacetime topology.
notes.conclusion: Biological-clock measurements are separate from relativistic clocks.
notes.confidence: Bounded to publisher/archival summary; not a full-text critical review

notes.label: Wormhole chronology versus actual spacetime engineering
notes.summary: Morris, Thorne and Yurtsever describe a conditional route from a traversable wormhole to a time machine, assuming such a wormhole can be constructed and maintained.
notes.limitations: The abstract itself flags weak-energy and quantum-gravity uncertainties. It does not report the creation of a traversable wormhole or demonstrate backward time travel.
notes.conclusion: Adds a conditional theoretical challenge to the research syllabus, but no empirical discrimination of physical histories.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review

notes.label: GRW objective-collapse dynamics
notes.basis: American Physical Society journal abstract · https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.34.470
notes.summary: Ghirardi, Rimini and Weber propose a modified dynamical model that aims to recover microscopic quantum behavior and classical localization for macroscopic systems.
notes.limitations: A formulated alternative is not by itself experimental confirmation; the relevant tests require precise collapse parameters and constraints.
notes.conclusion: Provides a serious competing mechanism for measurement outcomes without proving or refuting Everett branches.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review

notes.label: Extended Wigner-friend experimental assumptions
notes.basis: Science Advances / PubMed research abstract · https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aaw9832
notes.summary: Proietti and collaborators describe a six-photon extended Wigner-friend experiment and a Bell-type inequality violation tied to observer-independent-facts assumptions.
notes.limitations: The inference is conditional on assumptions including locality and free choice, and does not amount to an experimental observation of travel or interaction between alternate histories.
notes.conclusion: Observer-independent descriptions face nontrivial assumptions; no physically realized branching census is established.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review

notes.label: Large-molecule quantum interference constraints
notes.summary: Fein and colleagues report matter-wave interference involving molecules exceeding 25 kDa and discuss tests that constrain modifications to quantum mechanics.
notes.limitations: Molecular interferometry is not an observation of multiple universes; experimental methods and collapse-model bounds need detailed full-text examination.
notes.conclusion: Raises priority for the chemistry and quantum-foundations cross-lab without shifting the history-count verdict.
notes.confidence: Scoped to accessible abstract; no full text or independent replication review
